feedback: The confession follows my leading inference: Artie's denial tried to remove the accessible bottle from the timeline, while his admitted private-place visit supplied the glass opportunity. It adds his actual transfer of poison and explanation of the public argument, but those describe the crime rather than introducing a new forensic identifier needed for the vote. Chip's admission over the date and Monet's wage diversion resolve their separate lies cleanly. Emotionally, Artie's loss of the ability to manage the museum's account is fitting. I still think another actor could have performed the same physical route on the released facts, so the finale validates a plausible interpretation more strongly than it proves an exclusive one.
